annotation.title_clean: Trust and Accountability in Autonomous Robotic Systems
annotation.title_en: Trust and Accountability in Autonomous Robotic Systems
annotation.venue: Journal of Ethics in Emerging Technologies & Society
annotation.summary_en: Journal article proposing the Robot Trust and Accountability Framework (RoTAF) and a Trust-Accountability Quality Score (TAQS). It assesses five trust dimensions and four accountability mechanisms across six robot deployment contexts. Surgical robots score highest because medical accountability frameworks are strong. Eldercare robots score lowest, with no specific EU framework covering them. Over-trust is the most common problem across contexts.
key_provisions_or_claims: Physical embodiment makes trust calibration and accountability more consequential than for software-only AI.
Surgical robots have the highest TAQS (0.724) due to MDR, FDA and professional liability; eldercare robots the lowest (0.484).
There is no specific EU framework for care and companion robots, and their classification under the EU AI Act Annex III is uncertain.
Over-trust (automation bias) is the most prevalent trust problem in all deployment contexts.

Accountability mechanisms covered are product liability, professional accountability, incident investigation (AI Act Art. 73) and certification (ISO 10218, CE marking). Emergency response robots are currently ungoverned.
